## The client {#sec-project-client}

**ContactEase Solutions** is an Italian software house based in Bologna,
founded in 2016 by developers coming from mobile applications. It builds light
personal-productivity tools — address books, agendas, note managers, small
synchronisation utilities — for private users, freelancers and micro-companies
who want simple, fast solutions without needless complexity. Its catalogue
includes desktop and mobile applications and command-line utilities, partly
open source, under a mixed freemium/business-support model. About forty people
work in development, design and support, with short release cycles and strong
attention to code quality and clarity of the user experience.

Its guiding values are **ease of use**, **protection of the users' personal
data** (kept on the device whenever possible) and **maintainable,
well-documented code** — a principle the company applies to its internal
prototypes too.

### Didactic guidance

The goal is a command-line phone-book prototype in Python that applies
object-oriented principles correctly. The value of the work lies not only in
making the operations work, but in the **cleanliness of the architecture**:
classes with clear responsibilities, coherent methods, readable and commented
code. The user experience at the terminal (clear messages, understandable
menu) and robustness against wrong input matter too. Six operational tips
accompany the brief:

1. **Separate responsibilities between classes** — a `Contact` class for the
   single record (first name, last name, phone, optional e-mail) and a
   `PhoneBook` class managing the collection and its operations; keep the
   user-interaction logic **outside** the domain classes.
2. **Choose the data structure with care** — list, dictionary or a
   combination: assess what makes search and modification more efficient, and
   motivate the choice in a comment or a text cell.
3. **Make persistence reliable** — serialise objects to a readable format such
   as JSON; on loading, handle a missing or corrupted file without
   interrupting execution.
4. **Do not let the program crash** — use validation and `try`/`except` for
   non-numeric input, non-existent indices, empty fields. A prototype that
   ends with a traceback makes a terrible impression in a demo.
5. **Take care of the menu and the messages** — a main loop with numbered
   options, a confirmation after every operation, a clean way to exit that
   saves the data.
6. **Mind the Colab notebook** — interactive input works in Colab, but
   organise the cells so that the evaluator can run the code and try the menu
   smoothly; add a short demonstration of use.

## Design {#sec-project-design}

### Responsibilities

Following the guidance (and @sec-solid), the program splits into four
responsibilities, each a class (or module, @sec-real-package):

```{mermaid}
%%| echo: false
%%| fig-cap: "Architecture of the phone book. Arrows are dependencies; the graph is acyclic (@thm-toposort) and the domain does not depend on the interface."
flowchart LR
    UI["ConsoleUI<br/>(menu, input, messages)"] --> BOOK["PhoneBook<br/>(collection, rules)"]
    UI --> STORE["JsonStorage<br/>(load / save, file format)"]
    BOOK --> MODEL["Contact<br/>(one record, validation)"]
    STORE --> MODEL
```

- **`Contact`** — one record; validates its own fields (non-empty name, valid
  phone number) so that an invalid contact cannot exist (a class invariant,
  @sec-encapsulation).
- **`PhoneBook`** — the collection and its rules: no duplicates, sorted
  listing, search, edit, delete. No `input`, no `print`.
- **`JsonStorage`** — the only component that knows the file format
  (information hiding, @sec-modularity): loading tolerates a missing, empty or
  corrupted file; saving is atomic.
- **`ConsoleUI`** — the only component that talks to the user.

### The data structure, with its costs

What operations dominate? Listing (sorted), adding with a duplicate check,
searching by name, editing and deleting. Two candidates:

| Operation | `list` of contacts | `dict` keyed by identity `(name, surname, phone)` |
|---|---|---|
| duplicate check on add | $O(n)$ scan | $O(1)$ expected (@thm-chaining) |
| add | $O(1)$ amortised + $O(n)$ check | $O(1)$ expected |
| delete a known contact | $O(n)$ (find + shift) | $O(1)$ expected |
| search by substring of name | $O(n)$ | $O(n)$ |
| sorted listing | $O(n\log n)$ (or $O(n)$ if kept sorted) | $O(n \log n)$ |

: Costs of the two candidate structures ($n$ contacts) {#tbl-project-structures}

A **dict keyed by an identity tuple** makes the rule "no two identical
contacts" cheap and explicit, and Python dicts keep insertion order
(@sec-dicts); the sorted view is produced on demand with `sorted` (Timsort,
@sec-sorting). Substring search is linear either way (a prefix index or a
trie would be needed to do better — irrelevant for a personal phone book with
hundreds of entries, where every operation takes microseconds). **Motivation
for the notebook**: *"a dict gives $O(1)$ duplicate checks and deletions; at
the scale of a personal phone book the difference is negligible, so the
decisive reasons are clarity of the uniqueness rule and simplicity of the
code."* That is exactly the kind of justification tip 2 asks for.

### What identifies a contact?

Two entries are "the same contact" if they have the same name, surname and
phone number, ignoring letter case and spacing in the number. Homonyms with
different numbers are allowed (two different "Mario Rossi"). This identity is
an **equivalence relation** (@def-equivalence) because it is equality of a key
tuple; the sort order is lexicographic on `(surname, name, phone)`, a strict
total order on keys (@thm-lex-order).

### Robustness and user experience

- Every input goes through a small set of **validated readers** (`ask_text`,
  `ask_choice`, `ask_yes_no`) that loop until the input is valid
  (@sec-try) and are **injected** into the UI, so the UI can be tested with
  scripted input.
- Editing and deleting select a contact **from a numbered list of search
  results**, instead of asking the user to retype the whole contact exactly.
- <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd> or end of input (`EOFError`) **save and exit**
  instead of showing a traceback.
- Saving is **atomic** (@sec-atomic-writes): a crash during the save never
  destroys the phone book.

## Walkthrough of the published implementation {#sec-project-walkthrough}

The notebook in `ai-projects` is organised in four cells: the `Contatto`
class, the `Rubrica` class, the Google Drive mount, and the main program. The
class and method names are in Italian (the menu is generated from them); the
notebook includes a glossary.

**`Contatto`** stores first name, last name, number and country code
(`prefisso`, default 39). Its constructor converts number and country code with
`int(...)` and turns a failure into a clear `ValueError`. It defines `__eq__`
(all four fields equal) and `__lt__`, which compares the tuples
`(cognome, nome)` — so `list.sort()` orders contacts by surname, then name. A
helper `input_valid_contact()` reads a contact from the keyboard, looping on
`int(input(...))` until the number and country code are numeric.

**`Rubrica`** wraps a list (`self._rubrica`), initialised with the `None`
sentinel idiom to avoid the mutable-default trap (the code comment explains
why). It offers `aggiungi_contatto` (add, refusing exact duplicates via
`cerca_contatto`), `visualizza_contatti` (sort, then print), `modifica_contatto`
(read the contact to edit, then the replacement, refusing duplicates),
`elimina_contatto`, and `ricerca_contatto` (a sub-menu to search by name or by
number). Persistence: `load_file_in_rubr` reads the JSON list and rebuilds the
contacts; `convert_rubr_dict` turns contacts into dicts using
`inspect.signature(Contatto.__init__)` to discover the field names;
`load_rubr_in_file` writes the JSON with `indent=4`.

**The menu** is built dynamically: `functionlaties()` lists, with `dir(self)`,
the public method names that are not in an exclusion list, and the main loop
prints them numbered, reads a choice, checks it with `assert`, and calls the
method with `getattr(rubr, name)()` — a dispatch table built by introspection
(@sec-first-class). The loop ends on `esci` (exit), after which the phone book
is saved.

**What it does well**: OOP structure with two classes; special methods for
equality and ordering; the mutable-default idiom; validation loops on numeric
input; handling of `JSONDecodeError`; docstrings on every method; persistence
that round-trips; a menu that cannot drift out of sync with the methods.

### Code review: refinements suggested by this book

| # | Observation | Why it matters | Suggested change | Chapter |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Phone numbers stored as `int` | leading zeros are lost (`06…` → `6…`); `+`, spaces impossible | store a validated, normalised **string** (E.164) | @sec-casting, @sec-verification |
| 2 | `__eq__` defined without `__hash__` | contacts are unhashable: no sets/dict keys, duplicate checks stay $O(n)$ | define `__hash__` on the same key, or use a frozen dataclass | @prp-hash-contract |
| 3 | `Rubrica` reads `contatto._nome` etc. | breaks encapsulation of `Contatto` | public read-only attributes or properties | @sec-encapsulation |
| 4 | `input_valid_contact` has no `self` and calls `input()` inside the domain class | works only when called on the class; mixes UI and domain (against tip 1) | move it to the UI layer (or at least `@staticmethod`) | @sec-dataclasses, @sec-solid |
| 5 | `cerca_contatto`, `cerca_name` print messages | domain methods with UI side effects; hard to test | return results; let the UI print | @sec-return |
| 6 | `assert` used to validate the menu choice | disabled by `python -O` → `IndexError` | an explicit `if` with a message | @sec-assert |
| 7 | `os.path.exists` before `open` | LBYL with a race window; an **empty** file raises `JSONDecodeError` and is reported as invalid | EAFP on `FileNotFoundError`; treat empty as an empty book | @exm-toctou |
| 8 | Files opened without `encoding=` | accented names may break on another OS | `encoding="utf-8"` | @sec-text-vs-binary |
| 9 | Save with mode `"w"` | a crash mid-save truncates the file | atomic write (temp file + `os.replace`) | @sec-atomic-writes |
| 10 | Menu built from `dir()` | order is alphabetical, labels derive from method names, renaming a method changes the UI | an explicit dispatch table (label → function) | @sec-first-class |
| 11 | Edit/delete require retyping the whole contact | error-prone UX; the notebook's own to-do notes the "name exists but number differs" case | pick from a numbered list of search results | @sec-project-design |
| 12 | `Ctrl+C` / end of input | a traceback, and unsaved data | catch `KeyboardInterrupt`/`EOFError`, save, exit | @sec-try |
| 13 | Data structure choice not motivated in the notebook | tip 2 asks for it explicitly | a text cell with the analysis of @tbl-project-structures | @sec-choosing-collection |
| 14 | No automated tests | regressions go unnoticed | a small test suite with scripted input | @sec-verification |

: Code review of the published implementation {#tbl-project-review}

None of these prevents the prototype from working — it passed the course
assessment. They are the difference between a prototype and a product, which is
exactly the next step ContactEase is considering.

## Reference implementation {#sec-project-reference}

The code below applies all the refinements. It is written as four blocks that
correspond to the four modules of @sec-real-package (`models`, `book`,
`storage`, `cli`); in a notebook each block is one cell, in a package one file.

### `models`: the contact

```{python}
"""models — the Contact record and its validation."""
from __future__ import annotations
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict

_SEPARATORS = " -.()"

def normalize_phone(text: str, default_cc: str = "39") -> str:
    """Return the number as '+<8..15 digits>' (E.164 style); see Chapter 14."""
    s = "".join(ch for ch in str(text).strip() if ch not in _SEPARATORS)
    if s.startswith("+"):
        body = s[1:]
    elif s.startswith("00"):
        body = s[2:]
    else:
        body = default_cc + s
    if not re.fullmatch(r"\d+", body):
        raise ValueError(f"invalid characters in phone number: {text!r}")
    if not 8 <= len(body) <= 15:
        raise ValueError(f"a phone number needs 8-15 digits including the country code: {text!r}")
    return "+" + body

_EMAIL = re.compile(r"^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$")      # deliberately simple

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Contact:
    """One phone-book entry. Instances are always valid (class invariant).

    Identity (for duplicates): name, surname (case-insensitive) and phone.
    Sort order: surname, name, phone (case-insensitive).
    """
    name: str
    surname: str
    phone: str
    email: str = ""

    def __post_init__(self):
        # frozen dataclass: use object.__setattr__ to store the normalised values
        name, surname, email = self.name.strip(), self.surname.strip(), self.email.strip()
        if not name:
            raise ValueError("the first name must not be empty")
        if email and not _EMAIL.match(email):
            raise ValueError(f"invalid e-mail address: {email!r}")
        object.__setattr__(self, "name", name)
        object.__setattr__(self, "surname", surname)
        object.__setattr__(self, "email", email)
        object.__setattr__(self, "phone", normalize_phone(self.phone))

    @property
    def identity(self) -> tuple[str, str, str]:
        return (self.name.casefold(), self.surname.casefold(), self.phone)

    @property
    def sort_key(self) -> tuple[str, str, str]:
        return (self.surname.casefold(), self.name.casefold(), self.phone)

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        full = f"{self.name} {self.surname}".strip()
        extra = f"  <{self.email}>" if self.email else ""
        return f"{full:<28} {self.phone}{extra}"

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        return asdict(self)

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, d: dict) -> "Contact":
        return cls(name=d["name"], surname=d.get("surname", ""),
                   phone=d["phone"], email=d.get("email", ""))

c = Contact(" Ada ", "Lovelace", "+44 20 7946 0000", "ada@example.org")
print(Contact("Mario", "Rossi", "06 1234 5678"))       # Italian landline: +39 added, leading 0 kept
print(c, "|", c.identity)
```

### `book`: the collection and its rules

```{python}
"""book — the PhoneBook: a collection of unique contacts. No input/print here."""
from typing import Iterator

class PhoneBookError(Exception):
    """Base class of phone-book errors."""

class DuplicateContactError(PhoneBookError):
    pass

class ContactNotFoundError(PhoneBookError, LookupError):
    pass

class PhoneBook:
    """Unique contacts, stored in a dict keyed by identity.

    Invariant: no two stored contacts have the same identity.
    Costs (n contacts): add/remove/contains O(1) expected; listing O(n log n);
    search O(n).
    """
    def __init__(self, contacts: list[Contact] | None = None):
        self._by_id: dict[tuple, Contact] = {}
        for c in contacts or []:
            self.add(c)

    def add(self, c: Contact) -> None:
        if c.identity in self._by_id:
            raise DuplicateContactError(f"{c.name} {c.surname} ({c.phone}) is already in the phone book")
        self._by_id[c.identity] = c

    def remove(self, c: Contact) -> None:
        try:
            del self._by_id[c.identity]
        except KeyError:
            raise ContactNotFoundError(str(c)) from None

    def replace(self, old: Contact, new: Contact) -> None:
        """Edit: replace old with new, keeping the no-duplicates invariant."""
        if old.identity not in self._by_id:
            raise ContactNotFoundError(str(old))
        if new.identity != old.identity and new.identity in self._by_id:
            raise DuplicateContactError(f"{new.name} {new.surname} ({new.phone}) already exists")
        del self._by_id[old.identity]
        self._by_id[new.identity] = new

    def search(self, text: str) -> list[Contact]:
        """Contacts whose first or last name contains text (case-insensitive), sorted."""
        t = text.strip().casefold()
        return [c for c in self if t in c.name.casefold() or t in c.surname.casefold()]

    def search_phone(self, text: str) -> list[Contact]:
        target = normalize_phone(text)
        return [c for c in self if c.phone == target]

    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[Contact]:
        return iter(sorted(self._by_id.values(), key=lambda c: c.sort_key))

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self._by_id)

    def __contains__(self, c: object) -> bool:
        return isinstance(c, Contact) and c.identity in self._by_id
```

### `storage`: reliable JSON persistence

```{python}
"""storage — the only module that knows the file format (information hiding)."""
import json, os, tempfile
from pathlib import Path

class CorruptedFileError(PhoneBookError):
    pass

class JsonStorage:
    def __init__(self, path: str | Path):
        self.path = Path(path)

    def load(self) -> tuple[list[Contact], list[str]]:
        """Return (contacts, warnings). Missing or empty file -> empty phone book."""
        try:
            text = self.path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        except FileNotFoundError:                       # EAFP: no race window
            return [], [f"{self.path.name} not found: starting with an empty phone book"]
        if not text.strip():
            return [], [f"{self.path.name} is empty: starting with an empty phone book"]
        try:
            records = json.loads(text)
        except json.JSONDecodeError as err:
            raise CorruptedFileError(f"{self.path.name} is not valid JSON") from err
        contacts, warnings = [], []
        for i, rec in enumerate(records if isinstance(records, list) else []):
            try:
                contacts.append(Contact.from_dict(rec))
            except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError) as err:   # skip bad records, keep the rest
                warnings.append(f"record {i} skipped: {err}")
        return contacts, warnings

    def save(self, contacts) -> None:
        """Atomic write: temporary file in the same folder, then os.replace."""
        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=self.path.parent, prefix=self.path.name, suffix=".tmp")
        try:
            with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                json.dump([c.to_dict() for c in contacts], f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
                f.flush()
                os.fsync(f.fileno())
            os.replace(tmp, self.path)
        except BaseException:
            os.unlink(tmp)
            raise
```

### `cli`: the console user interface

```{python}
"""cli — all interaction with the user lives here."""

class ConsoleUI:
    MENU = [("List all contacts", "list_all"), ("Add a contact", "add"),
            ("Search by name", "search"), ("Search by phone number", "search_by_phone"),
            ("Edit a contact", "edit"), ("Delete a contact", "delete"),
            ("Save and exit", None)]

    def __init__(self, book: PhoneBook, storage: JsonStorage, input_fn=input, print_fn=print):
        self.book, self.storage = book, storage
        self.input, self.print = input_fn, print_fn          # injected: testable without a keyboard

    # ---- validated readers -------------------------------------------------
    def ask_text(self, prompt: str, required: bool = True, default: str = "") -> str:
        while True:
            text = self.input(prompt).strip()
            if text or not required:
                return text or default
            self.print("  This field cannot be empty.")

    def ask_choice(self, prompt: str, n: int) -> int:
        while True:
            text = self.input(prompt).strip()
            if text.isdigit() and 1 <= int(text) <= n:
                return int(text)
            self.print(f"  Please type a number between 1 and {n}.")

    def ask_yes_no(self, prompt: str) -> bool:
        while True:
            text = self.input(prompt + " [y/n] ").strip().casefold()
            if text in ("y", "yes", "s", "si", "sì"):
                return True
            if text in ("n", "no"):
                return False
            self.print("  Please answer y or n.")

    def ask_contact(self, current: Contact | None = None) -> Contact:
        """Read a valid contact; with `current`, an empty answer keeps the old value."""
        while True:
            hint = (lambda v: f" [{v}]") if current else (lambda v: "")
            name = self.ask_text(f"First name{hint(current.name if current else '')}: ",
                                 required=current is None, default=current.name if current else "")
            surname = self.ask_text(f"Last name{hint(current.surname if current else '')}: ",
                                    required=False, default=current.surname if current else "")
            phone = self.ask_text(f"Phone{hint(current.phone if current else '')}: ",
                                  required=current is None, default=current.phone if current else "")
            email = self.ask_text(f"E-mail (optional){hint(current.email if current else '')}: ",
                                  required=False, default=current.email if current else "")
            try:
                return Contact(name, surname, phone, email)
            except ValueError as err:                       # the model validates; the UI explains
                self.print(f"  Invalid contact: {err}. Please try again.")

    def pick(self, candidates: list[Contact]) -> Contact | None:
        if not candidates:
            self.print("  No matching contact.")
            return None
        for i, c in enumerate(candidates, start=1):
            self.print(f"  {i}) {c}")
        return candidates[self.ask_choice("Which one? ", len(candidates)) - 1]

    # ---- features ----------------------------------------------------------
    def list_all(self):
        if len(self.book) == 0:
            self.print("  The phone book is empty.")
        for c in self.book:
            self.print(f"  {c}")

    def add(self):
        try:
            self.book.add(self.ask_contact())
            self.print("  Contact added.")
        except DuplicateContactError as err:
            self.print(f"  Not added: {err}.")

    def search(self):
        results = self.book.search(self.ask_text("Text to search in first/last name: "))
        self.print(f"  {len(results)} result(s).")
        for c in results:
            self.print(f"  {c}")

    def search_by_phone(self):
        try:
            results = self.book.search_phone(self.ask_text("Phone number: "))
        except ValueError as err:
            self.print(f"  {err}")
            return
        for c in results or []:
            self.print(f"  {c}")
        if not results:
            self.print("  No contact with this number.")

    def edit(self):
        old = self.pick(self.book.search(self.ask_text("Who do you want to edit? ")))
        if old is None:
            return
        self.print("  Press Enter to keep the current value.")
        new = self.ask_contact(current=old)
        try:
            self.book.replace(old, new)
            self.print("  Contact updated.")
        except DuplicateContactError as err:
            self.print(f"  Not updated: {err}.")

    def delete(self):
        victim = self.pick(self.book.search(self.ask_text("Who do you want to delete? ")))
        if victim and self.ask_yes_no(f"  Delete {victim.name} {victim.surname}?"):
            self.book.remove(victim)
            self.print("  Contact deleted.")

    # ---- main loop -----------------------------------------------------------
    def run(self):
        self.print(f"Phone book: {len(self.book)} contact(s) loaded.")
        try:
            while True:
                self.print("\nMENU")
                for i, (label, _) in enumerate(self.MENU, start=1):
                    self.print(f"  {i}) {label}")
                label, action = self.MENU[self.ask_choice("Choose an option: ", len(self.MENU)) - 1]
                if action is None:
                    break
                getattr(self, action)()
        except (KeyboardInterrupt, EOFError):
            self.print("\nInterrupted.")
        finally:                                            # always save on the way out
            self.storage.save(self.book)
            self.print(f"Saved {len(self.book)} contact(s) to {self.storage.path.name}. Bye!")

def main(path: str = "phonebook.json") -> None:
    storage = JsonStorage(path)
    try:
        contacts, warnings = storage.load()
    except CorruptedFileError as err:
        print(f"Error: {err}. The file was left untouched; fix or rename it and restart.")
        return
    for w in warnings:
        print("Note:", w)
    ConsoleUI(PhoneBook(contacts), storage).run()
```

### A demonstration of use

In Colab or a terminal you would simply call `main()`. To make the
demonstration reproducible in this book we **inject** a scripted sequence of
answers instead of the keyboard (@sec-try) — including several deliberate
mistakes — and print the session transcript.

```{python}
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

workdir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
book_file = workdir / "phonebook.json"

def scripted(answers):
    it = iter(answers)
    def fake_input(prompt=""):
        answer = next(it)                 # raises StopIteration -> we convert to EOFError below
        print(f"{prompt}{answer}")
        return answer
    def safe_input(prompt=""):
        try:
            return fake_input(prompt)
        except StopIteration:
            raise EOFError
    return safe_input

session_1 = [
    "9", "abc", "2",                                   # invalid menu choices, then "Add"
    "Ada", "Lovelace", "+44 20 7946 0000", "ada@example.org",
    "2", "Grace", "Hopper", "+1 202 555 0100", "",     # add, no e-mail
    "2", "Alan", "Turing", "12ab", "",                 # invalid phone -> asked again
    "Alan", "Turing", "+44 161 496 0000", "",
    "2", "ada", "LOVELACE", "0044 20 7946 0000", "",   # same as Ada (case, 00 prefix) -> refused
    "1",                                               # list
    "7",                                               # save and exit
]
contacts, notes = JsonStorage(book_file).load()        # first start: file missing
print("Notes:", notes)
ConsoleUI(PhoneBook(contacts), JsonStorage(book_file), input_fn=scripted(session_1)).run()
```

Second session: the phone book is reloaded from the file, a contact is
edited and another deleted, and the session ends abruptly (end of input),
which still saves.

```{python}
session_2 = [
    "5", "turing", "1", "", "", "", "alan.turing@example.org",   # edit Alan: keep fields, add e-mail
    "6", "hop", "1", "maybe", "y",                               # delete Grace (after an invalid answer)
    "3", "LOVE",                                                 # search
    "1",
    # no more input: simulates Ctrl+D -> EOFError -> save and exit
]
contacts, notes = JsonStorage(book_file).load()
print("Loaded:", len(contacts), "contacts; notes:", notes)
ConsoleUI(PhoneBook(contacts), JsonStorage(book_file), input_fn=scripted(session_2)).run()
print("\nFile content:\n" + book_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
```

### Tests

A handful of automated checks for the behaviours the brief cares about
(@sec-verification). In a real project they would live in
`tests/test_phonebook.py` and run with `pytest`.

```{python}
def expect(exc, fn, *args):
    try:
        fn(*args)
    except exc:
        return True
    return False

tests = {}
# Contact validation
tests["phone keeps leading zero"] = Contact("A", "B", "06 1234 5678").phone == "+390612345678"
tests["invalid phone rejected"] = expect(ValueError, Contact, "A", "B", "12ab")
tests["empty name rejected"] = expect(ValueError, Contact, "  ", "B", "3331234567")
# PhoneBook invariant
b = PhoneBook([Contact("Mario", "Rossi", "3331112222")])
tests["duplicate refused (case-insensitive)"] = expect(DuplicateContactError, b.add, Contact("mario", "ROSSI", "+39 333 111 2222"))
b.add(Contact("Mario", "Rossi", "3339998888"))
tests["homonym with other number allowed"] = len(b) == 2
tests["edit into duplicate refused"] = expect(DuplicateContactError, b.replace,
    Contact("Mario", "Rossi", "3339998888"), Contact("Mario", "Rossi", "3331112222"))
tests["sorted listing"] = [c.surname for c in PhoneBook([Contact("Z", "Zeta", "3330000001"),
                            Contact("A", "Alfa", "3330000002")])] == ["Alfa", "Zeta"]
# Storage
tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
tests["missing file -> empty book"] = JsonStorage(tmp / "none.json").load()[0] == []
(tmp / "empty.json").write_text("", encoding="utf-8")
tests["empty file -> empty book"] = JsonStorage(tmp / "empty.json").load()[0] == []
(tmp / "bad.json").write_text("[{", encoding="utf-8")
tests["corrupted file -> clear error"] = expect(CorruptedFileError, JsonStorage(tmp / "bad.json").load)
s = JsonStorage(tmp / "round.json"); s.save(b)
tests["save/load round trip"] = set(c.identity for c in s.load()[0]) == set(c.identity for c in b)
(tmp / "mixed.json").write_text('[{"name": "Ok", "phone": "3331234567"}, {"name": "Bad", "phone": "x"}]', encoding="utf-8")
loaded, warns = JsonStorage(tmp / "mixed.json").load()
tests["bad records skipped, good kept"] = len(loaded) == 1 and len(warns) == 1

for name, ok in tests.items():
    print(f"{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}  {name}")
print(f"{sum(tests.values())}/{len(tests)} tests passed")
```

### How the reference implementation meets the brief

| Requirement | Where |
|---|---|
| R1, R5, R10 interactive menu, confirmations, clean exit that saves | `ConsoleUI.run`, `MENU`, `finally: save` |
| R2, R3 OOP, separated responsibilities, UI outside the domain | `Contact`, `PhoneBook`, `JsonStorage`, `ConsoleUI` |
| R4 motivated data structure | `PhoneBook._by_id` + @tbl-project-structures |
| R6 add, list, edit, delete, search | `ConsoleUI.add/list_all/edit/delete/search/search_by_phone` |
| R7, R8 JSON persistence; missing/empty/corrupted file | `JsonStorage.load/save` (EAFP, atomic) |
| R9 no crash on wrong input | `ask_text`, `ask_choice`, `ask_yes_no`, `ask_contact`, `EOFError` handling |
| R11 commented code, demo of use | docstrings and comments; the scripted sessions above |

## Extensions {#sec-project-extensions}

1. **Package and command line.** Split the four blocks into the package layout
   of @sec-real-package and add an `argparse` entry point
   (`phonebook --file book.json --search Rossi`, @sec-argv).
2. **Faster search.** Keep a sorted list of `sort_key`s and use binary search
   (`bisect`, @sec-binary-search) for prefix search by surname in
   $O(\log n + m)$ for $m$ results. Prove the bound.
3. **Import/export CSV** (@sec-csv) so the phone book can be opened in a
   spreadsheet, with correct quoting of names containing commas.
4. **Undo.** Keep a stack of inverse operations (add ↔ remove, replace ↔
   replace back) and add an *undo* menu entry.
5. **Fuzzy search.** Match names with typos using `difflib.get_close_matches`
   (standard library).
6. **SQLite backend.** Implement a `SqliteStorage` with the same interface as
   `JsonStorage` (an abstract base class `Storage`, @sec-inheritance) and
   switch backends without touching the UI — the payoff of information hiding.
7. **AI-assisted review.** Give an assistant the brief and your code as a
   structured prompt (@sec-structured-prompting) and ask for a review and for
   additional edge-case tests; verify each suggestion before accepting it.
